body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-28 on the published `:dev` image (sha256:380243dab830) booted against a POPULATED
pre-feature app.db (9 users, 662 annotations, 234 kobo_synced) taken from a prod backup.

First boot after upgrade prints:

    [Migration] Warning: Could not update duplicates sidebar setting:
      (sqlite3.OperationalError) no such column: user.has_own_library
    [Migration] Warning: Could not update favorites sidebar setting: (same)

Mechanism: the duplicates-sidebar migration (cps/ub.py ~2151) and the favorites-sidebar migration
(~2183) both query `User` through the ORM. The ORM emits SELECT for every column the MODEL declares,
including `has_own_library` - which the My Library migration does not ALTER in until ~2257. So on any
database that predates the feature, those two migrations raise, are swallowed by a broad
`except Exception`, and skip. Their markers are not written, so they retry on the next boot, by which
time the column exists, and they then apply correctly (VERIFIED: after one restart, favorites=1 for all
9 users and duplicates=1 for exactly the 5 admins, both markers written).

So it is self-healing after one restart, and the damage on a single upgrade is limited to stale sidebar
bits plus two warnings that read like data corruption and are not.

The reason to fix it is structural rather than this instance: **any migration placed before a column-add
that ORM-queries that table breaks the same way, and the broad except swallows it just as quietly.**
The next one may not be as harmless as a sidebar bit.

Fix shape: additive column migrations for a model must run BEFORE any migration that ORM-queries that
model - i.e. hoist the has_own_library / user_library_seeded / my_library_intro_dismissed ALTERs to the
top of the sequence. Cheap and it removes the class. A narrower alternative is to make schema-touching
migrations use raw SQL rather than the ORM, which is more invasive.

Also worth noting for whoever picks this up: NO existing gate could see it. 7,360 unit tests build the
schema in memory so the column always exists; the local e2e rig, main's E2E lane and CI integration all
boot a FRESH app.db with no pre-existing users to migrate. It needs a populated pre-feature database -
FAILURE-MODES class 6 - which is exactly the configuration nobody was running.
title: Adding a column to the User model breaks every earlier migration that ORM-queries User
